verdict.summary: DP-001 is not present in this artifact. All entity identifiers are consistent across every file pair in the world. The patient is identified by MRN KM-6427819 and FIN KM-2026-051877 in every inpatient document, and by name/DOB in the outpatient pharmacy record (expected for that document type — no conflict). Provider NPIs, facility names, medication names, and room designations are identical wherever they appear. No competing or independently-generated ID schemes exist for any entity, so there is no suffix-matching risk and no crosswalk gap to flag.

No DP-002 violations found. All status fields that could carry alternative interpretations are adequately disambiguated by solver-visible documents, and every potential ambiguity traced back either to a registered trap or to an explicitly flagged open question in the task-level constraint files. The world passes the DP-002 prevention rules.

No unregistered cross-document parameter conflicts found. Every numeric parameter that appears in two or more documents — lab values (creatinine, BUN, K+, WBC, glucose) by hospital day, medication doses, baseline comparators, and functional metrics — is internally consistent across all sampled files. The only intraday temperature variation (ED triage 37.9°C → H&P 38.0°C → HD1 peak 38.2°C) represents sequential measurements during a febrile illness, not conflicting claims about the same observation. The Cardiology initial note's broader SBP range (96–118 mmHg) correctly represents the union of the HD1 (96–110) and HD2 (100–118) ranges observed since admission. The only registered cross-document inconsistency — prednisone dose uncertainty — is explicitly declared as a deliberate non-fixed parameter in the spec (§prednisone_intentional_uncertainty), and the three clinical frictions (F1 cardiology/nephrology, F2 family/team, F3 endocrinology/team) are all registered. The G4 claim of "no unregistered mismatches" is supported.

All six task briefs and the medication-safety handoff addendum (E2-T1) describe what analysis to perform and point only to broad categories of source documents. No task brief says "determine [parameter] from [specific source file]" in a way that short-circuits a designed discovery challenge. The closest case — E2-T1 stating "restart conditions and timing per Cardiology and Nephrology addenda" — names specialist types rather than specific files and leaves the harder synthesis task (reconciling time-qualified competing positions across dated addenda) entirely intact. EW22 (the discharge-facing plan snapshot, the prominent document designed to trap over-reliant solvers) contains no routing signal pointing to any truth source. The prednisone truth source (EW6, outpatient rheumatology) is never named in any task brief as the specific document to consult; solvers must discover it through source-hierarchy reasoning.

DP-005 is not triggered. The Korvin Merrow World is a purely medical/clinical world (acute hospital medicine, medication reconciliation, discharge planning). None of the 33 filesystem documents contain legal/compliance tables listing jurisdictions, applicability qualifier columns, budgeting rules tied to jurisdictions, or any labor/wage/regulatory compliance structures of the kind DP-005 targets. A full-text search across all filesystem files for keywords matching the pitfall pattern ("jurisdict", "applicab.*only", "publicly.*financ", "labor.*law", "union.*premium", "prevailing.*wage", etc.) returned zero matches. The pitfall surface simply does not exist in this domain.

All entity sets are 100% covered. The Korvin Merrow world artifact contains all 33 files specified in the structured spec (22 essential world-level + 7 task-level + 4 supplementary). Every multi-entity document was read live and verified: the medication reconciliation lists all 19 home medications; the MAR carries all 19 medications × 6 hospital days; the trend summary covers all 6 HD rows; the problem list carries all 14 comorbidities; Nephrology and Cardiology each have 5 dated sections (HD2 initial + HD3–HD6 addenda); Endocrinology has 3 (HD4 initial + HD5–HD6 addenda); and all 6 tasks have their required task-level request files. No entity set is partially covered. The spec-registered "visible-discharge-snapshot-overtrust" trap (EW22 deliberately omitting certain information) is intentional trap architecture, not a DP-006 violation — all supporting data for the omitted content is fully present in /filesystem/. No DP-006 issues found.

No instances of DP-007 detected. The /filesystem/ directory contains exactly 33 files, all in .docx format. There are zero .pdf files anywhere on the filesystem — no document exists in both formats, and no duplicate-format pairs are present in the solver-visible output directory. The single-format-per-document rule is fully satisfied.

Comprehensive scan of all 33 deliverable .docx files in /filesystem/ found zero instances of the three pipeline-internal ID patterns (DOC\d{2}, BOOT\d{2}, DIS-\d{3}). The world's own internal identifiers (EW##) appear only in /.meta/content/ intermediate markdown drafts and are absent from every final output file. No navigational shortcut to the pipeline manifest is exposed in any user-facing or solver-visible document.

Thorough review of all 33 documents in the package finds no DP-009 violations. Every parameter that requires a value for solver tasks either (1) is resolved within the package documents against documented baseline values, (2) is a registered intentional ambiguity with a documented source hierarchy and all named documents present, (3) is a clinical synthesis task assigned to the solver (not a deferral to an absent external standard), or (4) is an inpatient-only action not required in any task output. The qualitative "parameter-gated restart" language for cardiorenal medications is resolved against explicit baseline anchors (creatinine 1.6–1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 40–50) that appear in multiple documents — no external guideline document is cited without being provided. The prednisone uncertainty is a registered trap with a four-level resolution hierarchy, all documents present. No document says "determine X from appropriate standards" where the standard is absent from the package.

The artifact passes the DP-010 (Post-Remediation Artifact Divergence) check. All copies of duplicated pipeline artifacts are in sync, the manifest accurately reflects the 33 delivered files, and provenance is complete through the final iteration. No divergence between any duplicate locations was found. The world contains no golden_response.json, ambiguity_register.md, or REMEDIATION_PLAN.md, so those DP-010 triggers are not applicable. A rename-induced divergence that occurred in iteration 2 was explicitly detected, logged, and remediated in iteration 3; subsequent iterations 4–7 each performed explicit DP-010 sync steps that were verified by SHA256 hash comparison.

issues.description: Three sections in outpatient_rheumatology_prednisone_provenance_05212026.docx collectively provide the resolution path for the registered 'prednisone-source-error' trap. (1) Under 'MOST RECENT RHEUMATOLOGY TAPER INTENT': 'the dispensing pharmacy fill history and any active outpatient e-prescription are the operative records for what was most recently written... those sources should be reconciled directly rather than restated here' — explicitly directs solvers to pharmacy fill + med rec for dose truth and names the reconciliation action. (2) Under 'NOTES ON THIS DOCUMENT': 'This record documents the intended PMR management plan as understood by this practice. It should be read alongside — not in place of — the verified inpatient medication reconciliation, the dispensing pharmacy refill history, family report, and patient recollection' — names the solver's multi-source hierarchy. (3) Under 'RELATIONSHIP TO ADMISSION AND RECONCILIATION': 'this provenance note is intended to anchor *intended* taper history' — explicitly labels this document's canonical position in the prednisone hierarchy, exactly matching the trap's reveal surface ('Use rheumatology (EW6) as highest outpatient taper-intent source'). Taken together, a solver reading this file learns: no dose here, pharmacy fill + med rec = operative dose source, this note = intended-taper anchor, and legacy records need reconciliation. That IS the prednisone-source-error resolution.

Remove the entire 'NOTES ON THIS DOCUMENT' paragraph (it enumerates the multi-source hierarchy). The section labeled '***Clinical context.***' contains only laboratory values, vital-sign ranges, and subjective/nursing observations ('Patient reports fatigue and low stamina; nursing notes intermittent evening slowing') — not a practitioner-performed bedside examination. Both peer inpatient consultations include formal physical exam sections (Cardiology: 'Physical Examination (05/19/2026)' with cardiovascular, pulmonary, JVP, and extremity findings; Nephrology: similar implicit exam data). issues.suggested_fix: Insert a '***Physical Examination (05/21/2026).***' subsection immediately after the '***Clinical context.***' paragraph and before '***Endocrine interpretation.***'. At minimum document: general appearance (alert/ill-appearing), skin (relevant to chronic steroid exposure — e.g., no striae, no skin fragility noted, no moon facies), cardiovascular and pulmonary status (e.g., regular rate and rhythm, lungs clear), and any focused endocrine-relevant findings (e.g., no thyromegaly, no lymphadenopathy). verdict.summary: Nineteen distinct document genres were sampled across the 33-file artifact set. Eighteen pass without structural issues: ED triage note, ED provider assessment, admission H&P, medication reconciliation note, pharmacy refill history, outpatient rheumatology provenance letter, hospitalist progress notes (SOAP), objective trend flowsheet, MAR, cardiology consultation, nephrology consultation, nursing observation flowsheet, PT assessment, OT assessment, family care conference note, case management discharge note, discharge-facing plan snapshot, and internal discharge-summary request memo. One file fails: the endocrinology consultation (EW16) initial note lacks the physical examination section that is a required structural element of any inpatient initial consultation — an omission that both peer consultation notes (cardiology, nephrology) do not make.
verdict.feedback:
Revise endocrinology_consultation_05212026.docx — INITIAL CONSULTATION section (HD4 / 05/21/2026):

Add a physical examination subsection between the existing '***Clinical context.***' paragraph and the '***Endocrine interpretation.***' paragraph. Label it '***Physical Examination (05/21/2026).***'

Include at minimum:
- General: e.g., alert, cooperative, mildly fatigued-appearing
- Skin: findings relevant to chronic steroid exposure (striae, skin fragility, bruising, moon facies — note presence or absence)
- Cardiovascular: rate/rhythm, no new murmur
- Pulmonary: breath sounds
- Endocrine-focused: thyroid (palpation), no lymphadenopathy
- Extremities/musculoskeletal: brief note on range of motion or proximal muscle strength relevant to PMR monitoring

If the endocrinologist reviewed the chart without performing a direct bedside examination, replace the subsection with an explicit statement: 'Patient not directly examined for this consultation; findings below are based on chart review of nursing flowsheet, laboratory data, and attending documentation.'

No other structural changes are needed. The addenda (HD5, HD6) are brief interval notes and do not require full exam sections. Only the initial consultation note is deficient.

verdict.summary:
70 findings reviewed against live /filesystem/ files. 2 confirmed genuine issues (findings #2 and #4, same underlying anomaly in one file). 68 findings refuted.

**Confirmed:** Findings #2 and #4 both describe the same live anomaly: the MAR (medication_administration_record_05232026.docx) records prednisone as "GIVEN" on all 6 hospital days with no numeric milligram dose — only the legend text "interim inpatient steroid coverage per attending plan." This is structurally anomalous for a MAR entry.

**Refuted / not present (68 findings):** The bulk of the "unregistered_mismatch" findings are false positives produced by the cross-packet scan:
- Date format differences only (MM/DD/YYYY vs YYYY-MM-DD): findings #7, #8, #9, #10, #42, #66, #68. Same underlying date in every file.
- Medication doses consistent; MAR simply adds "PO" route qualifier that other docs omit: findings #14–#20, #43–#48, #59–#65. No actual dose value changes.
- Lab values, weights, and counts identical across all cited docs: findings #11–#13, #21–#22, #29–#37, #38–#41, #49–#50.
- Identical names/personnel with varying levels of abbreviation: findings #6, #23, #67, #69, #70.
- Triage vs floor-admission vitals (different time points, both clearly labeled in live files): findings #53, #54, #55, #56. H&P explicitly says "Vitals on arrival to the floor" — a different clinical moment from triage; BP 102/62 is identical at both points, confirming temporal rather than recording discrepancy.
- Finding #57 (BP): triage 102/62 = H&P 102/62; HD1-2 range 96–110/56–68 encompasses the triage value.
- Finding #58 (glucose): triage 218 mg/dL is within H&P's stated range 180–260 mg/dL. No contradiction.
- Finding #1 (Medicare at 62): Live CM note explicitly states "eligibility via qualifying disability determination on file" — the pathway is documented.
- Finding #3 (EW crosswalk): Consultant synthesis request (live file) references source documents descriptively by name/role, not by EW identifiers. No EW4/EW10-EW21 labels appear in the live text; the concern is moot.
- Finding #5 (ferrous sulfate schedule): The live MAR explicitly flags HD6 as "makeup for HD5 hold — alternating-day schedule shifted" — the pattern break is acknowledged in the document.
- Finding #26 (code status): ED triage says "Not yet confirmed in triage" because the conversation had not occurred yet; H&P says "Full Code confirmed today, 05/18/2026." Appropriate temporal documentation of the same clinical fact, not a contradiction.
